01 / Predictions

One well. Three approaches.

Train: 1 Jan–30 May 2026 (150 days). Test: 31 May–29 Jun (30 days). Every model receives the actual future drivers it uses: M1 none; M2 rain; M3 volume, rain, supply and demand. This is a conditional-input test.

02 / Errors

Separate data quality from model complexity.

25 wells deliberately acquire measurement bias. All models see biased readings, while scoring uses the physical truth. Omitting these wells changes the evaluation population; it does not solve drift.

03 / Overall comparison

Each model answers a different data situation.

QuestionM1 · Real-data trendM2 · Rainfall scenarioM3 · 450-well driver

What this proves

On this constructed system, static readings remove most of the dynamic-reading error. Drivers improve the remaining forecast and enable ordered pumping/rain scenarios. The same test exposes sensor drift.

What this does not prove

It does not establish Bengaluru accuracy, sustainable yield, aquifer recharge rates, or six-month to five-year reliability. Synthetic data favour their generating assumptions. Future drivers remain uncertain and drift requires calibration evidence.

Data-readiness path

M1 · Available now
Screened pump sessions and a clear dynamic-level definition.

M2 · Add public rainfall
Well locations and longer overlapping observations for real lag testing.

M3 · Company data contract
Standard static readings, calibration, pumped volume, supply/demand, nearby activity and ≥6–12 months of history.
